concepts.def: Transmission of tunes and songs by ear rather than notation, producing regional variants and allowing each performer a personal version.
Sustained pitch or pair of pitches held beneath a melody, characteristic of bagpipe traditions and of the Indian tanpura.
Decorative additions such as slides, grace notes, rolls and mordents with which traditional performers personalise and vary a melody.
Many folk tunes use modes such as Dorian or Mixolydian rather than the major-minor system, giving them their distinctive colour.
Contemporary artists blend traditional material with jazz, classical, rock or electronic idioms; Piazzolla's tango nuevo fused tango with jazz and classical techniques.
A leader's phrase answered by a group or second player, a structural principle central to many African and other folk traditions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 6: Contemporary Traditional Music — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 6: Contemporary Traditional Music brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 6: Contemporary Traditional Music.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A sustained pitch held underneath a melody is called a what?
options: Riff
Drone
Cadence
Hook

mcqs.q: Astor Piazzolla's 'tango nuevo' fused Argentine tango with elements of which traditions?
options: Jazz and Western classical music
Gamelan and gagaku
Plainchant and organum
Twelve-tone serialism only

mcqs.q: Music passed on by ear from performer to performer is said to belong to what?
options: The oral tradition
The figured bass tradition
The serial tradition
The through-composed tradition

mcqs.q: A folk melody with a major third but a flattened seventh is most likely in which mode?
options: Dorian
Mixolydian
Aeolian
Lydian

mcqs.q: Does traditional music stay fixed and unchanged over time?
options: Dorian has no seventh degree at all.
Traditional music is frozen in the past and must always be played the same way.
Traditional music changes only when governments update it.
No - oral transmission produces constant variation, and contemporary artists keep reworking traditional material in new settings.

mcqs.q: What is a drone in traditional music?
options: A continuously sustained pitch (or pitches) that accompanies the melody, as on bagpipes or the tanpura.
A drone is a type of slow melody played in the low register.
A drone is the fastest dance section of a folk set.
Dorian has no seventh degree at all.

mcqs.q: How does the Dorian mode differ from the natural minor scale on the same tonic?
options: A drone is the fastest dance section of a folk set.
Dorian has no seventh degree at all.
Modes are just alternative names for the ordinary minor scale.
Dorian has a raised sixth degree compared with the natural minor; otherwise the two scales match.
